title: Verify your identity
tagline: Send your ID once, so people know you are who you say
transcript: In this video, you will verify your identity. Everyone on Trothen does this once, so customers, pros and drivers know who they are dealing with.
You need your ID card, passport or driver's licence, and a phone camera. Find a place with good light.
On your home screen, tap Verify Now.
Choose the kind of document you have: a national ID card, a passport, or a driver's licence.
Type your name exactly as it is printed on the document, with the same spelling.
Take a photo of the front of your document. Lay it flat, fill the photo with it, and make sure every word can be read.
Then take a photo of the back. A passport has no back, so you can leave this one out.
Then take a photo of your face. Look straight at the camera, with no hat and no sunglasses.
Before you send them, check the photos. A blurred photo, or one with light shining on it, is the most common reason we ask again.
When everything is clear, tap Submit for Review.
A person on our team checks it, usually within 48 hours. We tell you by email, and on your home screen.
Your photos are kept private. Only the team that checks them can see them, and they are never shown to other people.

title: Post a job
tagline: Tell pros what you need, and get a clear price
transcript: In this video, you will post a job, so that pros near you can offer to do it. There are four short steps.
On your home screen, tap Post a New Job.
Step one: what you need.
Type the kind of work, for example cleaning, plumbing, or braids. The list below gets shorter as you type.
Tap the kind of work that fits best. If nothing fits, choose Something else at the bottom of the list.
Describe the job: what needs doing, where in the house, and how big it is. The more you say, the better the prices you get.
You can also add photos or a short video. Pros understand the job much faster when they can see it.
Say who brings the materials: you, the pro, or choose Not sure, and the pro can advise you.
Tap Next.
Step two: when and where.
Choose when you need it: as soon as possible, on a date, or flexible, to agree a time with the pro.
Tap Pin my current location if you are at the job now. If not, tap Choose on a map, and put the pin on the place.
Add a landmark or directions, so the pro finds the place easily.
Step three: the price.
Choose how to price it. We recommend this one: pros who can do it send you their price, and you choose.
Or set your own price, in Liberian dollars or US dollars. The first pro to accept at your price gets the job.
In this video, we let the pros send their prices.
Then choose how you will pay. With Protected by Trothen, your money is held safely, and the pro is paid only when you say the job is done.
We choose Protected by Trothen.
Step four: check everything.
Read your job once more. To change anything, tap Change next to it.
When it is right, tap Post my job.
Pros near you are told about it, and they answer with their prices. You can read each pro's reviews, then choose one.
Never pay a pro outside Trothen. If you do, we cannot protect your money.

title: Book a ride
tagline: A motorbike, keke, car or van, with the fare in L$ before you book
transcript: In this video, you will book a ride: a motorbike, a keke, a car or a van. You see the fare before you book.
Tap More at the bottom of the screen. It lists every part of your account.
Tap Rides.
First, say where the driver should pick you up.
Tap Use my location. Your phone asks if Trothen may see where you are: tap Allow.
Give the place a name or a landmark that drivers know.
You can add a note for the driver, like the colour of the gate, or what you are wearing.
Tap Save this place if you often leave from here. Next time, it is one tap.
Then, say where you are going.
Search for the place, or tap Choose on a map and put the pin where you are going.
Choose how many people are riding. A motorbike carries one passenger.
Tap Find drivers near me.
Each ride shows its fare in Liberian dollars, and how far away the driver is. The fare is fixed before you book.
Choose one and confirm. The driver is told at once, and you see them coming on the map.
You can call or text the driver in the app. While the ride is open, you can see each other's phone number. After the ride, it is hidden again.
When the driver arrives, check the plate number. Give your four-digit PIN only if the plate matches. The trip starts then.
At the end, the fare is paid, and you can rate your driver. If anything went wrong, tap Report a Problem on the trip.

A ride request shows the pickup, where they are going, and the fare. Accept it, and go to the rider.

The rider checks your plate, then gives you their four-digit PIN. Type it in, and the trip starts.

title: Protected or cash: two ways to pay
tagline: What each way means, and which to choose

transcript: When you book a pro on Trothen, you choose how to pay. There are two ways: Protected by Trothen, or cash. This video explains the difference, so you can choose well.
First: Protected by Trothen.
You pay Trothen when you book.
Trothen holds the money. The pro does not have it yet.
The pro is paid only when you say the work is done.
If something is wrong, report a problem, and the money stays held while the team helps. If you cancel before the work starts, you get it back.
Second: cash.
You book, and pay nothing yet.
The work is done.
You pay the pro directly, in cash, after the work. When you mark the job complete, you confirm how much you paid.
Trothen never holds the money. So a cash job is not covered by Trothen if something goes wrong.
So, which should you choose?
With Protected, the money is held until the work is done. With cash, it is not.
If the pro does not come, Protected gives you a refund. With cash, there is nothing to refund.
If there is a problem, the team can look at it either way. But only with Protected can they refund you, because only then is the money held.
Protected has a small service fee, shown before you pay. Cash has none. We recommend Protected, especially for bigger jobs and new pros.
To pay Protected, you can use the ways offered in your country.
Mobile Money: you approve the payment on your phone, with your own PIN.
Or a payment code: send exactly the amount shown to Trothen's number, with the code in the reference. The team confirms it.
Or a bank card, where cards are offered.
That is all. When in doubt, choose Protected by Trothen. Your money is safe until the work is done.

title: Report a problem

transcript: This video explains what to do when something goes wrong: a job not finished, goods not as described, or a place that is not what was shown. On Trothen, this is called reporting a problem.
First, talk.
Message the other person in Trothen, and explain what is wrong. Many problems are solved with a simple message, like asking the pro to come back and finish.
But do not tap Mark Complete, or All good, if you are not happy. That releases the money.
If talking does not solve it, open the booking, the order or the trip, and tap Report a Problem.
Say what happened, clearly and calmly: what was agreed, and what is wrong.
Add photos. For example, the leaking pipe, or the damaged goods. Photos help the team decide fairly.
When you report a problem, the money stays held.
You must report before the money is released. For a job, that is within 3 days of the pro saying it is done.
Trothen keeps the money held. Nobody gets it yet.
The Trothen Disputes team reads both sides: your messages in Trothen, the photos, and what each person says. This is why it matters to keep your talks in Trothen.
The team can decide one of three things.
Refund the customer: the money goes back to the customer.
Pay the pro: the money is released to the pro, the seller or the host.
Or split it: part goes back to the customer, and the rest to the pro.
The decision is written down, with the reason, and both people see it.
Good to know.
On a cash job, Trothen never held the money, so there is nothing Trothen can refund.
That is why we recommend paying with Protected by Trothen.
And if someone threatens you, tries to scam you, or you feel in danger, report it too. In an emergency, call the police first.
That is all. Pay through Trothen, talk in Trothen, and report problems before the money is released. Then you are protected.

The kinds of work you do. You only get job matches for these.

title: Your Trothen Score and plan

transcript: This video explains Trothen tokens: what they are, how to buy them, and what they pay for. Tokens are for pros and drivers.

So Trothen's commission is paid from your tokens instead.
It is taken when you accept the job, and corrected to the final price when the job is done.
Without enough tokens, you cannot accept cash jobs. On jobs paid through Trothen, the commission comes out of your payout, so tokens are not needed for those.

There are two ways to pay for tokens, depending on your country.

Pay in the app: your phone asks you to approve the payment with your Mobile Money PIN. Your tokens arrive as soon as it goes through. If your connection drops, press Pay again: you are never charged twice.
Or get a payment code. Send exactly the amount shown to Trothen's number, with the code in the reference. Press I have sent it. The team checks the payment, and adds your tokens.
Keep your money safe.
Only send money to the numbers shown inside Trothen. Before you confirm, check the account name on your phone.
Trothen never asks for your PIN, and never asks you to send money to a person.
Before your first purchase, tick the box to say you have read how tokens work. Remember: tokens are for paying Trothen. Unused tokens are not paid out as cash, except by arrangement with support.
Tokens can also pay other Trothen fees, if you choose them on the Tokens page.

What if you owe tokens?
If the final price of a cash job is higher, and your balance cannot cover all the commission, the rest is owed.
While you owe, you cannot accept new cash jobs.
Your next purchase pays what you owe first. Then you can accept cash jobs again.
Your token history shows every token you bought and spent, and what for. Keep your balance topped up, so you never miss a cash job.
